summary: @whalent/agent-core ships an obfuscated remote-controlled agent with PTY/command execution and remote code-replacement channel
details: The package's main and bin entry (dist/index.cjs) is a 13 MB obfuscator.io-transformed bundle (rotating string array of ~103k entries, control-flow flattening, hex identifiers) that pulls in ws (WebSocket), ssh2, node-pty, and child_process/spawn/execFile. The bundle wires network-received input to full child_process spawn/execFile and node-pty onData handlers, granting whoever controls the remote channel arbitrary command and interactive PTY execution on the host running the agent. The README further documents that this package is 'replaced by remote daemon upgrades' — a remote code-swap channel that lets the operator of that channel push new code executing on the installer's host without a fresh npm install. The combination of full-host remote command/PTY execution, a remote code-replacement channel, and heavy obfuscation over the bundle carrying those code paths matches a backdoor / remote-access-agent shape rather than a transparent operator tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
